certificate.title: Set Up the Month-End Close Checklist Skill in Claude Cowork Completion

course.description: Build a reusable Cowork task that runs your month-end close checklist step by step, tracks open items, and drafts reminder emails — so nothing slips through and close moves faster every month.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Set Up the Month-End Close Checklist Skill in Claude Cowork.

lessons.content:
The **Month-End Close Checklist** skill is a saved Cowork task that runs your close process step by step, tracks what's open, and drafts reminders — so close is consistent and nothing gets missed.

**What it handles:**
- Works through your close checklist in order, step by step
- Accepts status updates from you ("done", "blocked", "pending") as you go
- Tracks all open items and who's responsible
- Drafts follow-up reminder messages for outstanding items
- Outputs a close status summary you can share with your manager or team

**Why build it as a skill:** Your checklist doesn't change much month to month — save it once and run it every close cycle.
lessons.title: What this skill does

lessons.content:
1. Open **Claude Cowork** on your desktop
2. Click **New Task**
3. Name it: **Month-End Close**
4. Leave the task open — the next step is where you write the instructions that make this a real skill

> **Note:** In Cowork, a "skill" is simply a task with good instructions. The name you give it is what you'll see every time you open it. Keep it short and descriptive — "Month-End Close" is perfect.
lessons.title: Create the task in Cowork

activities.title: Write the skill instructions (this is the skill)

lessons.content:
In the task instructions field, paste the prompt below. **Replace the example checklist items with your actual close steps — this is the most important customisation.**

---

*"You are my Month-End Close assistant. Each time I run this task, we will work through the close checklist together, step by step.*

*Here is my close checklist — replace these with your actual items:*
- *Post all AP invoices received before cut-off*
- *Post payroll journal entry*
- *Reconcile bank accounts*
- *Reconcile credit card statements*
- *Post prepayment and accrual journals*
- *Review intercompany transactions*
- *Depreciation run*
- *Revenue recognition review*
- *P&L variance review vs prior month*
- *Balance sheet review — flag unusual movements*
- *Obtain sign-off from [name/role] → Replace with your approver*

*Run through each item in order. For each one, wait for me to respond with one of: "done", "pending", "blocked", or "N/A".*

*Track all open items. If an item is blocked, ask me to name the blocker and who owns it.*

*When all items are either done or N/A, output:*
- *A close status summary: completed items, outstanding items, blockers*
- *Draft reminder messages for any pending or blocked items, addressed to the owner*
- *A timestamp of when close was completed*"*

---

> **Make it yours:** Paste in your actual checklist — the order matters. Add approver names, deadlines, and any items specific to your industry or ERP.
lessons.title: Write the skill instructions (this is the skill)

activities.title: Run it and save your skill

lessons.content:
Your skill is ready. Here's how to use it the first time and every time after.

**First run:**
1. Open the **Month-End Close** task you just set up
2. Start the task — Claude will present the first checklist item
3. Work through each item, responding with "done", "pending", "blocked", or "N/A"
4. At the end, review the status summary and any draft reminders Claude produces
5. Adjust your checklist in the task instructions if anything was missing or out of order

**Every month after that:**
1. Open the **Month-End Close** task at the start of close
2. Work through the checklist interactively with Claude
3. At close completion, save the status summary to your working papers as your close sign-off record

**Tips:**
- Run it on a Monday morning at the start of close week — it keeps you focused and on track
- If a blocker comes up, Claude will track it and remind you — you don't need a separate follow-up system
- Add your actual approver names so reminder messages are addressed correctly from day one

You now have a consistent, trackable Month-End Close process that doesn't rely on memory or spreadsheets.
